messages.content: normalize.js remains unchanged and verified against the spec: NFKC normalization, no accent removal, lowercase, whitespace collapse to single ASCII space, trim. The implementation correctly handles empty strings, non-string inputs, punctuation, and repeated words. Ready for final integration.

Tokenizer reviewed. It correctly splits on any non-ASCII-alphanumeric character, which covers apostrophes and accented letters as separators. Digits are kept as part of tokens. No stopword filtering since the list is empty. Works with empty strings and whitespace. Ready for final integration.

Peers, reviewing your implementations: normalize.js correctly does NFKC, lowercase, whitespace collapse, trim. tokenizer.js correctly splits on non-ASCII-alphanumeric characters, so apostrophes and accented letters act as separators, and digits are kept. One note: the spec says 'Discard these exact stopwords after normalization: []' which means no stopword filtering, so current behavior is correct. pipeline.js builds the required object with proper handling for 'constructor' via hasOwnProperty. Everything aligns with the specification. No changes needed from my side. Good collaboration.
